title: Race rehearsal, 950m unbroken then 550m on tired legs
terrain: alpine, ~22km / 1500m D+, two climbs, two full descents

steps.target: Z1-Z2 full descent, controlled, short strides
Z2 second climb, ~550m D+, 152-161 bpm, legs already tired

coachNotes: Restructured around the 900m+ climb you have access to. Two climbs and two full descents beats one climb and a traverse, because Pirin is 3300m over 38km and no single ascent wins that race, the second and third ones do. Climb 1 unbroken at 89-93% LTHR, never above 167, and treat the first 45 minutes as deliberately too easy. Eat every 40 minutes from the first hour, this is a fuelling rehearsal as much as a fitness one. Climb 2 is the point of the session: it teaches you what hour four feels like. Both descents run at full length because your ITB has to be conditioned for 3300m of give-back and only descent volume does that. Hard abort: any lateral knee signal, skip climb 2, walk out, and Sunday drops to 60 flat. Start by 07:00, roughly 3h50 total. ALPS GATE, NOW LIVE: take the mean of your Wed 19, Thu 20 and Fri 21 morning RHR readings. That is your Alps baseline, call it B. Gate this session at the same offsets you used on Paros: green if RHR is at or below B+2, amber between B+3 and B+5 (drop climb 2 to 300m, load ~130), red at B+6 or above (climb 1 only at Z2, walk the descent, load ~80). For HRV stop using absolute numbers permanently and use the ratio: 7-day mean over 28-day baseline, green above 0.95, amber 0.90 to 0.95, red below 0.90. The ratio travels between locations, the absolute number does not. If you are sleeping above 1800m, extend the observation window to Saturday morning and widen amber by 2bpm: the first four or five nights at real altitude add 3 to 6bpm that is hypoxia, not fatigue, and gating on it would cost you the whole peak week for nothing.
